items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: I worked with Dion once or twice, we did some things

ctx.x: So going from artist to artist, how much of your love of early rock & roll influenced —

I guess, you know like I really love rock & roll, real rock & roll, and I really love what people call doo wop, the groups. My two favorite musics probably are doo wop and Gospel. And so when you love something you have a certain sensibility like I like to put strings and voices on and horns on a lot of the jazz records I made, the commercial ones, but the voices were always Cissy Houston and the Sweet Inspirations, because of work they had done with Aretha and because they were all out of the church. Cissy ran a…
And how did that happen in the studio? You invite these singers in? Is there a vocal arranger who works?
